description: Automate deployment of all Supabase edge functions in CI so Tessa never runs `supabase functions deploy` by hand, and update the two Spanish user docs to reflect Unsplash + hands-off deploy. The workflow must also trigger on changes under supabase/functions/** while still applying migrations, keep the concurrency guard, and reference only the specific existing secrets (never dump the environment).
steps: Edit .github/workflows/deploy.yml. Widen the push trigger `paths` to include BOTH 'supabase/migrations/**' and 'supabase/functions/**' so the workflow runs when either migrations or functions change on main. Keep branches: [main].
Keep the existing concurrency group 'desplegar-supabase' with cancel-in-progress: false so deploys never overlap.
Keep the existing migrations deploy (supabase link --project-ref + supabase db push) using secrets SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN, SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF, SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD and environment: production.

Add edge-function deployment to the SAME workflow. Preferred structure: in the existing job, after `supabase link` and `supabase db push`, add a step that deploys the functions; OR add a second job that also checks out, installs supabase/setup-cli@v1 (version: latest) and links with --project-ref. Either way reuse supabase/setup-cli@v1 and `supabase link --project-ref "${{ secrets.SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF }}"`. If you add a second job, it must share the concurrency group behavior appropriately and run after migrations (use `needs:`), so migrations and functions deploy coherently.

Deploy command: use the standard deploy (all functions validate their own JWT, so do NOT pass --no-verify-jwt). For CLI version 'latest', `supabase functions deploy` with no function name deploys all functions in supabase/functions/. To be robust across CLI versions, deploy each function explicitly by name: analyze-meal, discover-recipes, generate-recipe, recipe-photo, scan-ticket (e.g. a step running `supabase functions deploy <name> --project-ref "${{ secrets.SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF }}"` per function, or a short loop over those names). Add a comment explaining the explicit-name choice.

SECURITY HARD RULE: do NOT add any `env`/`printenv`/`set` dump, do NOT echo secret values, and reference only SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN, SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF, SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD. Mirror the existing env: block pattern (SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN as env for CLI auth). SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD is only needed for db push; do not expose it to steps that don't need it if you split jobs.

Keep all comments in Spanish and in the same friendly, explanatory tone as the current deploy.yml. Explain in a comment that edge functions now deploy automatically on merge to main so no manual `supabase functions deploy` is ever needed.
Validate the YAML parses (e.g. `python3 -c "import yaml;yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/deploy.yml'))"`). Do NOT break ci.yml or ai-development.yml.

Update docs/RECETAS_FOTOS.md: switch the whole guide from Pexels to Unsplash. New flow: (1) create a developer app on Unsplash (https://unsplash.com/developers), demo mode (50 req/hora) is enough, copy the 'Access Key'; (2) add it as a secret in the SUPABASE WEB PANEL (Edge Functions -> Secrets, or Project Settings -> Edge Functions -> Secrets) named EXACTLY UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY, no terminal; (3) nothing else - the function deploys itself via CI on merge to main. Remove the `supabase secrets set` and `supabase functions deploy` terminal commands. Keep the reassuring 'the app already works without this (cozy placeholder)' framing and the manual-photo note. Keep it in Spanish, no em dashes.

Update docs/CI_CD_SECRETS.md: (a) state that edge functions now deploy AUTOMATICALLY when changes land on main (no manual `supabase functions deploy`); (b) explain that the ONLY thing Tessa must do for recipe photos is add the UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY secret in the SUPABASE web panel (Edge Functions -> Secrets), one time, no terminal - distinguish this from the GitHub Actions repository secrets which remain for the Supabase CLI/migrations; (c) note that the Gemini-based functions (generate-recipe, discover-recipes, analyze-meal) that previously had to be deployed by hand will now also be deployed automatically by this workflow. Keep Spanish tone, no em dashes.
If README links to RECETAS_FOTOS.md or CI_CD_SECRETS.md, make sure those links still make sense; adjust surrounding text only if it now contradicts the new flow (do not do large rewrites).
acceptance_criteria: .github/workflows/deploy.yml triggers on push to main for changes under supabase/migrations/** OR supabase/functions/**.

The workflow still applies migrations (supabase db push) and additionally deploys all five edge functions by explicit name (analyze-meal, discover-recipes, generate-recipe, recipe-photo, scan-ticket) using supabase/setup-cli@v1 and supabase link --project-ref.
Only the existing secrets SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN, SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF, SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD are referenced; the workflow never dumps the environment or echoes secret values.
The concurrency group 'desplegar-supabase' is preserved and migrations/functions deploy in a coherent order.
deploy.yml, ci.yml, and ai-development.yml are all valid YAML.
docs/RECETAS_FOTOS.md describes the Unsplash flow with the only user action being adding UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY in the Supabase web panel (no terminal), in Spanish, no em dashes.
docs/CI_CD_SECRETS.md states edge functions deploy automatically on merge to main and that Tessa's only recipe-photo action is the UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY Supabase secret, in Spanish, no em dashes.
verification: Confirm deploy.yml paths include both supabase/migrations/** and supabase/functions/**.
Confirm the five functions are deployed by name and no env dump / secret echo exists.
Confirm docs mention UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY via Supabase web panel and auto-deploy.
findings: Implementado en el commit ad1cab0 sobre feat/recetas-rediseno. deploy.yml: paths ampliados a supabase/migrations/** y supabase/functions/**; job 'deploy' (migraciones) sin cambios de fondo; nuevo job 'deploy-functions' con needs: deploy, environment: production, que reinstala supabase/setup-cli@v1 (version: latest), hace supabase link --project-ref y despliega por nombre analyze-meal, discover-recipes, generate-recipe, recipe-photo, scan-ticket (sin --no-verify-jwt). deploy-functions NO expone SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD (solo SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN). concurrency 'desplegar-supabase' con cancel-in-progress:false conservada. Solo se referencian los tres secrets permitidos; no hay env/printenv/set dumps ni echo de secretos (verificado con grep). Los tres workflows parsean con pyyaml (hubo que pip install pyyaml en el sandbox). docs/RECETAS_FOTOS.md migrada de Pexels a Unsplash (demo 50 req/hora, UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY en panel web Supabase Edge Functions -> Secrets, sin terminal; eliminados supabase secrets set y functions deploy). docs/CI_CD_SECRETS.md: nuevas secciones sobre despliegue automatico de funciones en main y distincion entre repository secrets de GitHub y secrets de Edge Functions en Supabase; nota de que las funciones de Gemini tambien se despliegan solas. README.md: una linea cambiada de Pexels a Unsplash. No se toco codigo Dart, asi que no se corrio flutter build/test (cambios solo de YAML/docs).
